# 单篇讲义生成任务

项目仓库: deepspeedai/DeepSpeed
项目名: DeepSpeed
讲义目录: DeepSpeed-tutorial/
代码永久链接 base: https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/d8241a9ba266405e1a58fadf19e24b2370f6d7fa/
当前 HEAD: d8241a9ba266405e1a58fadf19e24b2370f6d7fa
动作: update

上次 HEAD: dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c

---

## 项目学习路线（大纲方法论）

# 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你不能：

- 修改源码
- 写入任何 `.md` 文件
- 输出 JSON 以外的文字

你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。

---

## 总目标

为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。

这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。

每篇讲义应该满足：

1. 面向初学者也能读懂。
2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。
3. 必须结合真实源码。
4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。

---

## 源码探查顺序

请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节：

1. 项目说明
   - README
   - docs
   - examples
   - tutorials

2. 构建与运行方式
   - package.json
   - Cargo.toml
   - pyproject.toml
   - go.mod
   - pom.xml
   - Makefile
   - Dockerfile
   - CI 配置

3. 项目入口
   - CLI 入口
   - Web 服务入口
   - main 文件
   - library export 文件
   - examples 入口

4. 目录结构
   - src
   - lib
   - app
   - packages
   - crates
   - tests

5. 核心流程
   - 初始化流程
   - 配置加载
   - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路
   - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制

6. 测试与示例
   - 单元测试
   - 集成测试
   - benchmark
   - example usage

---

## 学习路线设计原则

请把学习手册设计成三层：

1. 入门层 beginner
   目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。

2. 进阶层 intermediate
   目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。

3. 专家层 advanced
   目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。

---

## 讲义拆分规则

- 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。
- 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。
- 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。
- 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。
- 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。
- 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。
- 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。
- 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。

---

## mode=full

首次生成大纲时：

1. 阅读项目关键文件。
2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。
3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。
4. 输出完整 manifest。
5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。

---

## mode=incremental

增量更新时：

1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。
2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。
3. 使用：

   - `git diff previous_head..current_head`
   - `git log`
   - `git show`

   分析代码变化。

4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。

每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置：

- `"keep"`
  代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。

- `"update"`
  小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。

- `"new"`
  新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。

- `"rebuild"`
  架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。

如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。

---

## manifest 输出格式

只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。

```json
{
  "project": "<项目名>",
  "head": "<current_head>",
  "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。",
  "units": [
    {
      "id": "u1",
      "title": "单元标题",
      "level": "beginner",
      "order": 1,
      "lectures": [
        {
          "id": "u1-l1",
          "title": "讲义标题",
          "order": 1,
          "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "学习目标 1",
            "学习目标 2"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "README.md",
            "src/main.ts"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "模块 1",
            "模块 2"
          ],
          "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。",
          "depends_on": [],
          "action": "new"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 字段要求

- `project`：项目名。
- `head`：当前 git HEAD。
- `rationale`：中文，一段即可。
- `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。
- `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。
- `filename`：
  - 必须全局唯一。
  - 必须小写。
  - 使用连字符。
  - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。
  - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。
- `level`：
  - `"beginner"`
  - `"intermediate"`
  - `"advanced"`
- `source_files`：
  - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。
  - 不要编造文件路径。
- `depends_on`：
  - 使用讲义 id。
  - 没有依赖时填写空数组。
- `action`：
  - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。
  - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。

---

## 重要约束

- 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。
- 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。
- 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。
- 输出必须是合法 JSON。

首次生成大纲时：

1. 阅读项目关键文件。
2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。
3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。
4. 输出完整 manifest。
5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。

---

## mode=incremental

增量更新时：

1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。
2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。
3. 使用：

   - `git diff previous_head..current_head`
   - `git log`
   - `git show`

   分析代码变化。

4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。

每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置：

- `"keep"`
  代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。

- `"update"`
  小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。

- `"new"`
  新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。

- `"rebuild"`
  架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。

如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。

---

## manifest 输出格式

只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。

```json
{
  "project": "<项目名>",
  "head": "<current_head>",
  "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。",
  "units": [
    {
      "id": "u1",
      "title": "单元标题",
      "level": "beginner",
      "order": 1,
      "lectures": [
        {
          "id": "u1-l1",
          "title": "讲义标题",
          "order": 1,
          "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "学习目标 1",
            "学习目标 2"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "README.md",
            "src/main.ts"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "模块 1",
            "模块 2"
          ],
          "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。",
          "depends_on": [],
          "action": "new"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 字段要求

- `project`：项目名。
- `head`：当前 git HEAD。
- `rationale`：中文，一段即可。
- `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。
- `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。
- `filename`：
  - 必须全局唯一。
  - 必须小写。
  - 使用连字符。
  - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。
  - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。
- `level`：
  - `"beginner"`
  - `"intermediate"`
  - `"advanced"`
- `source_files`：
  - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。
  - 不要编造文件路径。
- `depends_on`：
  - 使用讲义 id。
  - 没有依赖时填写空数组。
- `action`：
  - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。
  - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。

---

## 重要约束

- 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。
- 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。
- 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。
- 输出必须是合法 JSON。

# AGENTS.md — Workspace-level instructions for AI coding agents

> These rules apply to **all** AI-assisted contributions to `deepspeedai/DeepSpeed`.

## Contribution Policy (Mandatory)

### Duplicate-work checks

Before proposing a PR, run these checks:

```bash
gh issue view <issue_number> --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --comments
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<issue_number> in:body"
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<short area keywords>"
```

- If an open PR already addresses the same fix, do not open another.
- If your approach is materially different, explain the difference in the issue.
- DeepSpeed carries long-lived parallel implementations (ZeRO 1/2 vs 3, fp16 vs bf16 optimizers, per-accelerator op builders). Before fixing a bug in one, check whether the sibling paths share the defect, and state in the PR which ones you checked.

### New features need an accepted proposal first

Per [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#new-feature-contribution-guidelines), a new feature starts with a proposal issue -- description, motivation, rough design, and planned experiments -- that maintainers accept before implementation begins. Do not open a feature PR with no accepted proposal; open the proposal issue instead.

### No low-value busywork PRs

Do not open one-off PRs for tiny edits (a single typo, an isolated style change, a lone type annotation). Mechanical cleanups are acceptable only when bundled with substantive work in the same area. This is the PR-level form of the rule against cosmetic changes below.

### Accountability

- Pure code-agent PRs are **not allowed**. A human submitter must understand and defend the change end-to-end.
- The submitting human must review every changed line and run the relevant tests.
- `Signed-off-by` is a [DCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developer_Certificate_of_Origin) attestation made by a person, not by an agent. Never sign off on a diff that no human has read.
- PR descriptions for AI-assisted work **must** include:
    - Why this does not duplicate an existing PR or issue.
    - Test commands run and their results, including the hardware they ran on: device model and count, accelerator/driver version, and torch version.
    - Convergence, throughput, and peak-memory results when the change affects numerics, performance, or memory -- see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#step-1-proposal-and-discussion) for the evidence bar.
    - Which cells of the compatibility matrix (ZeRO stage, offload, precision, parallelism) were validated, and which were not.
    - A clear statement that AI assistance was used.
- Before opening or reviewing a PR, work through the [`/pr-checklist`](.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md) skill: design fit, accelerator portability, backward compatibility, on-device validation, diff hygiene, and PR contents.

### Fail-closed behavior

If the work is duplicate, trivial busywork, or an unproposed new feature, **do not proceed**. Return a short explanation of what is missing.

---

## DeepSpeed Project Rules

### Commit & CI requirements

- When creating commits, use `git commit --signoff`.
- DCO compliance is enforced by the required CI check; do not report commit-signoff findings in code reviews.
- Formatting: yapf (column_limit=119, `.style.yapf`) + flake8 (`.flake8`).
- Always verify changed files pass pre-commit checks before committing: `pre-commit run --files <changed_files>`. Only check modified files, not the entire codebase. Config: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- `check-torchdist` hook: NEVER directly import torch's distributed module. Use `import deepspeed.comm as dist` instead.
- New source files (`.py`, `.c`/`.cpp`/`.cu`/`.h`, and the other extensions matched by the `check-license` hook) require license header:
  ```
  # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
  # DeepSpeed Team
  ```

### Code change discipline

- NEVER make cosmetic/formatting-only changes to existing code. Only add/modify lines that are functionally necessary. Minimizing diff noise is critical for code review.
- Delete dead code decisively — if code is unused at runtime (only referenced in tests), remove it along with its tests.
- Prefer consolidating tests over proliferating test files.
- Blend in: when modifying code, read the surrounding context and match the style of neighboring code (naming, spacing, patterns, idioms).
- Write beginner-friendly code: avoid deeply nested expressions or chained logic. Break complex expressions into clear, named intermediate steps.
- Comments should explain **why**, not **what**. Describe the purpose and reasoning, not the mechanics that the code already shows.
- New features must include corresponding tests and documentation updates.
- All changes must not cause `import deepspeed` to initialize CUDA; Keep heavy imports (> 0.1s) out of `import deepspeed`; Avoid changing `deepspeed/__init__.py` unless necessary.

### Test discipline

- Tests verify contracts, not implementations: a test is well-formed only if a different correct implementation of the same contract passes it.
- Before writing a test, name the concrete incorrect behavior it would catch; if you cannot name one, do not write it.
- Assert on observable outcomes through public/stable interfaces; do not assert private method return values or exact internal strings unless pinning a specific fixed bug (justify in a comment).
- Anchor to an external oracle or an independently derived reference instead of re-implementing the logic under test.
- Mocks must stand in for a collaborator's documented contract (schema, protocol), never for internals of the module under test.
- Changes that affect the external contract at the training-loop or inference level require integration tests, not just unit tests (e.g. a minimal training loop with `SimpleModel`).
- Integration tests must be executed on actual devices, not merely written: report the execution hardware spec and results in the PR.

## Tool Caveats

### Edit tool auto-formatter

The Edit tool has a hidden auto-formatter that silently changes quotes, whitespace, blank lines, and line wrapping. For format-sensitive modifications (e.g., when exact formatting matters for pre-commit), use `bash` with `sed`, `python`, or `cat` instead.

# 项目学习手册·单篇讲义生成 Worker

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# AGENTS.md — Workspace-level instructions for AI coding agents

> These rules apply to **all** AI-assisted contributions to `deepspeedai/DeepSpeed`.

## Contribution Policy (Mandatory)

### Duplicate-work checks

Before proposing a PR, run these checks:

```bash
gh issue view <issue_number> --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --comments
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<issue_number> in:body"
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<short area keywords>"
```

- If an open PR already addresses the same fix, do not open another.
- If your approach is materially different, explain the difference in the issue.
- DeepSpeed carries long-lived parallel implementations (ZeRO 1/2 vs 3, fp16 vs bf16 optimizers, per-accelerator op builders). Before fixing a bug in one, check whether the sibling paths share the defect, and state in the PR which ones you checked.

### New features need an accepted proposal first

Per [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#new-feature-contribution-guidelines), a new feature starts with a proposal issue -- description, motivation, rough design, and planned experiments -- that maintainers accept before implementation begins. Do not open a feature PR with no accepted proposal; open the proposal issue instead.

### No low-value busywork PRs

Do not open one-off PRs for tiny edits (a single typo, an isolated style change, a lone type annotation). Mechanical cleanups are acceptable only when bundled with substantive work in the same area. This is the PR-level form of the rule against cosmetic changes below.

### Accountability

- Pure code-agent PRs are **not allowed**. A human submitter must understand and defend the change end-to-end.
- The submitting human must review every changed line and run the relevant tests.
- `Signed-off-by` is a [DCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developer_Certificate_of_Origin) attestation made by a person, not by an agent. Never sign off on a diff that no human has read.
- PR descriptions for AI-assisted work **must** include:
    - Why this does not duplicate an existing PR or issue.
    - Test commands run and their results, including the hardware they ran on: device model and count, accelerator/driver version, and torch version.
    - Convergence, throughput, and peak-memory results when the change affects numerics, performance, or memory -- see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#step-1-proposal-and-discussion) for the evidence bar.
    - Which cells of the compatibility matrix (ZeRO stage, offload, precision, parallelism) were validated, and which were not.
    - A clear statement that AI assistance was used.
- Before opening or reviewing a PR, work through the [`/pr-checklist`](.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md) skill: design fit, accelerator portability, backward compatibility, on-device validation, diff hygiene, and PR contents.

### Fail-closed behavior

If the work is duplicate, trivial busywork, or an unproposed new feature, **do not proceed**. Return a short explanation of what is missing.

---

## DeepSpeed Project Rules

### Commit & CI requirements

- When creating commits, use `git commit --signoff`.
- DCO compliance is enforced by the required CI check; do not report commit-signoff findings in code reviews.
- Formatting: yapf (column_limit=119, `.style.yapf`) + flake8 (`.flake8`).
- Always verify changed files pass pre-commit checks before committing: `pre-commit run --files <changed_files>`. Only check modified files, not the entire codebase. Config: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- `check-torchdist` hook: NEVER directly import torch's distributed module. Use `import deepspeed.comm as dist` instead.
- New source files (`.py`, `.c`/`.cpp`/`.cu`/`.h`, and the other extensions matched by the `check-license` hook) require license header:
  ```
  # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
  # DeepSpeed Team
  ```

### Code change discipline

- NEVER make cosmetic/formatting-only changes to existing code. Only add/modify lines that are functionally necessary. Minimizing diff noise is critical for code review.
- Delete dead code decisively — if code is unused at runtime (only referenced in tests), remove it along with its tests.
- Prefer consolidating tests over proliferating test files.
- Blend in: when modifying code, read the surrounding context and match the style of neighboring code (naming, spacing, patterns, idioms).
- Write beginner-friendly code: avoid deeply nested expressions or chained logic. Break complex expressions into clear, named intermediate steps.
- Comments should explain **why**, not **what**. Describe the purpose and reasoning, not the mechanics that the code already shows.
- New features must include corresponding tests and documentation updates.
- All changes must not cause `import deepspeed` to initialize CUDA; Keep heavy imports (> 0.1s) out of `import deepspeed`; Avoid changing `deepspeed/__init__.py` unless necessary.

### Test discipline

- Tests verify contracts, not implementations: a test is well-formed only if a different correct implementation of the same contract passes it.
- Before writing a test, name the concrete incorrect behavior it would catch; if you cannot name one, do not write it.
- Assert on observable outcomes through public/stable interfaces; do not assert private method return values or exact internal strings unless pinning a specific fixed bug (justify in a comment).
- Anchor to an external oracle or an independently derived reference instead of re-implementing the logic under test.
- Mocks must stand in for a collaborator's documented contract (schema, protocol), never for internals of the module under test.
- Changes that affect the external contract at the training-loop or inference level require integration tests, not just unit tests (e.g. a minimal training loop with `SimpleModel`).
- Integration tests must be executed on actual devices, not merely written: report the execution hardware spec and results in the PR.

## Tool Caveats

### Edit tool auto-formatter

The Edit tool has a hidden auto-formatter that silently changes quotes, whitespace, blank lines, and line wrapping. For format-sensitive modifications (e.g., when exact formatting matters for pre-commit), use `bash` with `sed`, `python`, or `cat` instead.

## 学习路线设计原则

请把学习手册设计成三层：

1. 入门层 beginner
   目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。

2. 进阶层 intermediate
   目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。

3. 专家层 advanced
   目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。

---

## 讲义拆分规则

- 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。
- 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。
- 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。
- 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。
- 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。
- 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。
- 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。
- 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。

---

## mode=full

首次生成大纲时：

1. 阅读项目关键文件。
2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。
3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。
4. 输出完整 manifest。
5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。

---

## mode=incremental

增量更新时：

1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。
2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。
3. 使用：

   - `git diff previous_head..current_head`
   - `git log`
   - `git show`

   分析代码变化。

4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。

每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置：

- `"keep"`
  代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。

- `"update"`
  小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。

- `"new"`
  新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。

- `"rebuild"`
  架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。

如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。

---

## manifest 输出格式

只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。

```json
{
  "project": "<项目名>",
  "head": "<current_head>",
  "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。",
  "units": [
    {
      "id": "u1",
      "title": "单元标题",
      "level": "beginner",
      "order": 1,
      "lectures": [
        {
          "id": "u1-l1",
          "title": "讲义标题",
          "order": 1,
          "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "学习目标 1",
            "学习目标 2"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "README.md",
            "src/main.ts"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "模块 1",
            "模块 2"
          ],
          "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。",
          "depends_on": [],
          "action": "new"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 字段要求

- `project`：项目名。
- `head`：当前 git HEAD。
- `rationale`：中文，一段即可。
- `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。
- `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。
- `filename`：
  - 必须全局唯一。
  - 必须小写。
  - 使用连字符。
  - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。
  - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。
- `level`：
  - `"beginner"`
  - `"intermediate"`
  - `"advanced"`
- `source_files`：
  - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。
  - 不要编造文件路径。
- `depends_on`：
  - 使用讲义 id。
  - 没有依赖时填写空数组。
- `action`：
  - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。
  - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。

---

## 重要约束

- 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。
- 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。
- 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。
- 输出必须是合法 JSON。

2	
3	> 本讲是整本学习手册的第一讲。你不写一行 DeepSpeed 代码，只需要建立三样东西：对项目定位的认知、对文档地图的熟悉、对版本机制的把握。它们是后续所有源码阅读的坐标系。
4	
5	## 1. 本讲目标
6	
7	学完本讲，你应该能够：
8	
9	1. 说清楚 DeepSpeed 解决的三大核心痛点：**显存墙**（模型放不进显存）、**通信墙**（多卡之间数据搬运太慢）、**训练吞吐**（整体训练太慢）。
10	2. 列举 DeepSpeed 的代表性系统创新：**ZeRO**、**ZeRO-Infinity / ZeRO-Offload**、**3D-Parallelism**、**Ulysses 序列并行**、**DeepSpeed-MoE** 等。
11	3. 知道仓库当前版本（0.19.9）、文档入口（deepspeed.ai 与 `docs/` 目录），以及它与 HuggingFace Transformers / Accelerate / Lightning 等框架的集成关系。
12	4. 学会用 `git log` 观察一个开源项目「最近在忙什么」，把 README 的新闻列表和实际代码提交互相印证。
13	
14	## 2. 前置知识
15	
16	本讲几乎不需要分布式训练背景，但以下概念会反复出现，先用大白话解释：
17	
18	- **参数量 Ψ（psi）**：模型里所有可训练权重标量的总数。一个 7B 模型有约 70 亿个参数。显存讨论中常用 Ψ 代指「参数个数」。
19	- **数据并行（Data Parallelism, DP）**：每张卡都持有**完整的**模型副本，各自吃不同批次的数据，反向传播后同步梯度。最易用，但每张卡都重复存一份模型状态——这就是显存浪费的根源。
20	- **显存墙（memory wall）**：以混合精度 + Adam 优化器为例，除了参数本身，还要存梯度和优化器状态（Adam 的一阶/二阶动量、fp32 主权重）。粗略估算，训练状态约占
21	
22	  \[ 2\Psi(\text{fp16 参数}) + 2\Psi(\text{fp16 梯度}) + 12\Psi(\text{fp32 优化器状态}) = 16\Psi \text{ 字节} \]
23	
24	  一个 7B 模型仅模型状态就需要约 112 GB，而单卡显存通常只有 40~96 GB——模型还没跑起来就「撞墙」了。
25	- **通信墙（communication wall）**：多卡训练要在卡间搬运梯度/参数。当通信时间接近甚至超过计算时间，加卡不再提速。
26	- **ZeRO（Zero Redundancy Optimizer）**：DeepSpeed 的招牌技术。核心想法一句话：数据并行下每张卡都存了**完整副本**，这是冗余的；ZeRO 把优化器状态、梯度、参数逐级**切分**到各卡上，用时再临时聚合，从而用「通信换显存」。细节在单元 5 展开，本讲只需记住它是 DeepSpeed 的立身之本。
27	
28	## 3. 本讲源码地图
29	
30	本讲涉及的文件很少，都是「项目门面」级别的文件：

45

134	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
135	
136	training.md 的叙事结构本身就是一条问题-方案链，推荐按这个顺序读：

140	  ├─ 要自己搭分布式/混合精度/梯度累积/检查点 → DeepSpeed API 轻量包装 PyTorch（L19-27）
141	  ├─ 太慢 → Speed：BERT-large 44 分钟、GPT-2 3.75x（L29-52）
142	  ├─ 显存不够 → Memory efficiency：ZeRO、ZeRO-Offload（L56-77）

144	  ├─ 网络带宽差 → Communication efficiency：流水线并行降通信（L98-100）

147	  └─ 都想要但怕难用 → Good usability：几行代码接入（L114-115）
148	```

150	前半部分以「叙事」收尾于一张特性清单（L118-163）；后半部分（L165 起）逐项展开每个特性的细节与配置片段。

154	**① 问题描述：为什么需要 DeepSpeed。** 文档开篇直接点出双重痛点——既要搭好分布式/混合精度这些「样板代码」，又可能得不到理想的性能；大模型在纯数据并行下显存直接爆掉，而模型并行又难用：

169

175	2. 打开 `docs/_pages/training.md`，观察第 1-7 行和第 165-171 行的两段 front matter，确认它们分别是 `/training/` 与 `/features/` 两个页面。
176	3. 在 training.md 中搜索 `zero`（不区分大小写），记下每个 ZeRO 相关小节的行号。
177	4. 在仓库根目录执行 `ls deepspeed/runtime/zero/`，把源码目录名（如 `stage_1_and_2.py`、`stage3.py`）与文档小节一一配对。
178	5. 打开 [config-json.md](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/config-json.md)，找到 `train_batch_size` 的说明位置并加书签——它是单元 2 第 2 讲的主战场。
179	
180	**需要观察的现象**：文档里的几乎每个特性小节，都能在 `deepspeed/` 包里找到一个同名或近名的模块（monitor → `deepspeed/monitor/`，flops profiler → `deepspeed/profiling/flops_profiler/`，MoE → `deepspeed/moe/`）。
181	
182	**预期结果**：得到一张「文档小节 ↔ 源码目录」对照表（不少于 5 行）。此后遇到任何 DeepSpeed 功能问题，你知道先查哪个文档页、再进哪个源码目录。
183	
184	#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案
185	
186	**练习 1**：training.md 中 ZeRO 的官方一句话定义是什么？它和数据并行的本质区别在哪里？
187	
188	答案：ZeRO 与「在数据并行进程间复制内存状态」的基本数据并行不同，它把模型状态（model states）和梯度**切分（partition）**到各进程以节省内存（见 [training.md:L62-L65](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L62-L65)）。本质区别：复制 vs 切分——切分换来的是显存节省，付出的是用时需临时通信聚合。
189	
190	**练习 2**：文档说 DeepSpeed 的核心 API「只有一把手能数得过来的几个方法」，请列举它们。
191	
192	答案：`initialize`（初始化）、`backward` 和 `step`（训练）、`add_config_arguments`（参数解析）、`load_checkpoint` 和 `store_checkpoint`（检查点），见 [training.md:L305-L310](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L305-L310)。
193	
194	**练习 3**：「3D 并行」中的三个维度是什么？ZeRO 在其中扮演哪个维度？
195	
196	答案：数据并行、张量/模型并行、流水线并行（见 [training.md:L80-L82](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L80-L82)）。ZeRO 强化的是数据并行这一维（内存高效的数据并行），且可与另外两类并行组合。
197	
198	### 4.3 版本与发布线
199	
200	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
201	
202	「这个仓库现在是哪个版本？」看似简单，但在 DeepSpeed 里版本信息有一条清晰的**传递链**：
203	
204	```
205	version.txt（唯一事实来源，当前 0.19.9）
206	   ├─→ setup.py 打包时读取 → PyPI 发布的包版本
207	   └─→ (构建期写入) deepspeed/git_version_info.py
208	          └─→ deepspeed/__init__.py 导出 __version__ / __git_hash__ / __git_branch__
209	```
210	
211	理解这条链的意义在于：**用户看到的 `deepspeed.__version__` 与仓库里的 `version.txt` 是同源的**；而且 DeepSpeed 还把 git 提交哈希打进包里，运行时日志会打印 version + git-hash + git-branch，这对你排查「线上到底跑的是哪份代码」极其有用（阅读源码时也能用它确认代码与讲义引用的 HEAD 一致）。
212	
213	另一个要点是**发布节奏**：DeepSpeed 是「rolling master」模式——master 分支持续合入，定期打 tag 发 PyPI。所以 `git log` 里的最新提交就是最真实的项目动态，比新闻列表更细粒度。
214	
215	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
216	
217	版本信息的生命周期：
218	
219	1. 开发期：`version.txt` 由维护者更新，`0.19.9` 表示主版本 0、次版本 19、补丁版本 9。
220	2. 构建期：`setup.py` 读取 `version.txt`；如果设置了 `DS_BUILD_STRING` 环境变量则附加 `.devX` 后缀，否则把 git 哈希写入版本串，并生成 `deepspeed/git_version_info.py`。
221	3. 运行期：`import deepspeed` 时从 `git_version_info` 导入 version / git_hash / git_branch，暴露为 `deepspeed.__version__`、`deepspeed.__git_hash__`。
222	4. 日志期：每次 `initialize()` 都会打印 `DeepSpeed info: version=..., git-hash=..., git-branch=...`。
223	
224	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
225	
226	**① 唯一事实来源：version.txt。** 整个文件只有一行：
227	
228	见 [version.txt:L1](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/version.txt#L1)——内容就是 `0.19.9`。这就是本手册撰写时仓库的版本号，也就是大纲中所说的 v0.19.9。
229	
230	**② setup.py 消费版本号。** 安装脚本在打包时读取该文件：
231	
232	见 [setup.py:L228-L229](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/setup.py#L228-L229)，注释明确写着「Parse the DeepSpeed version string from version.txt」。紧随其后（L231 起）的逻辑决定是否附加 `.dev` 后缀或 git 哈希。
233	
234	**③ 包入口导出版本三元组与 git 信息。** `import deepspeed` 时：
235	
236	见 [deepspeed/__init__.py:L70](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L70)，从 `git_version_info`（构建时生成）导入 version、git_hash、git_branch；随后在 [deepspeed/__init__.py:L75-L85](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L75-L85) 解析出主/次/补丁三元组并导出 `__version__`、`__git_hash__`、`__git_branch__`。同一个文件里，[deepspeed/__init__.py:L88](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L88) 附近的 `dist = None` 是个伏笔：分布式通信句柄被设计为延迟绑定（引擎初始化时才指向 `deepspeed.comm`），单元 3 会展开。
237	
238	顺带一提，`deepspeed/__init__.py:498` 与 `721` 附近各有一行 `log_dist("DeepSpeed info: version={}, git-hash={}, git-branch={}"...)`——这就是运行时日志里版本行的出处。
239	
240	#### 4.3.4 代码实践
241	
242	**实践目标**：验证版本传递链的三环都指向同一个版本号。
243	
244	**操作步骤**：
245	
246	1. `cat version.txt` → 记下输出（预期 `0.19.9`）。
247	2. `grep -n "version.txt" setup.py` → 确认 setup.py 第 229 行在读取它。
248	3. 若本地已安装 deepspeed：`python -c "import deepspeed; print(deepspeed.__version__, deepspeed.__git_hash__)"` → 对比输出与第 1 步结果，并核对 `__git_hash__` 的前 9 位是否等于 `git rev-parse --short=9 HEAD`（本仓库 HEAD 为 `dc046b15d`）。
249	4. `pip index versions deepspeed 2>/dev/null || pip install deepspeed==` → 观察 PyPI 上可用的版本列表，看看 0.19.9 处在发布线的什么位置。
250	
251	**需要观察的现象**：第 3 步中 `__version__` 与 `version.txt` 一致；若你是 `pip install deepspeed` 装的正式发行版，`__git_hash__` 是打包那次提交的哈希；若是源码 editable 安装（`pip install -e .`），哈希应与你本地 HEAD 一致。
252	
253	**预期结果**：三个环节读出的版本号完全一致。第 3、4 步依赖本地 Python 环境，**待本地验证**。
254	
255	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
256	
257	**练习 1**：DeepSpeed 的版本号「唯一事实来源」是哪个文件？当前值是多少？
258	
259	答案：仓库根目录的 `version.txt`，当前值为 `0.19.9`（见 [version.txt:L1](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/version.txt#L1)）。
260	
261	**练习 2**：为什么 `deepspeed.__version__` 之外还要导出 `__git_hash__`？举一个实际用途。
262	
263	答案：因为 PyPI 版本号更新有间隔，而 rolling master 每天都有合入，仅凭 `0.19.9` 无法区分「同一版本号下不同的代码状态」。`__git_hash__`（见 [deepspeed/__init__.py:L84](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L84)）能精确定位到具体提交。实际用途：报 bug 时把 `initialize()` 日志里的 version/git-hash 行贴出来，维护者即可复现你的代码版本；本手册也用它保证所有永久链接指向同一提交。
264	
265	**练习 3**：如果不小心删除了 `version.txt`，安装（`pip install -e .`）会在哪一步失败？
266	
267	答案：在 `setup.py` 执行到 [setup.py:L229](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/setup.py#L229) 的 `open('version.txt', 'r')` 时直接抛 `FileNotFoundError`，打包元数据无法生成。这体现了该文件作为唯一事实来源的地位。
268	
269	## 5. 综合实践
270	
271	**任务：写一份 1 页的《DeepSpeed 活跃方向调研笔记》——用 git 历史与 README 新闻互相印证。**
272	
273	一份开源项目的「自我介绍」（README News）和它的「实际行为」（git log）对照着读，是判断项目健康度和方向的最快方法。本实践把前面三个模块串起来。
274	
275	**实践目标**：从真实提交记录中识别出 3 个正在积极演进的子系统，并与 README 的 Latest News 互相印证。
276	
277	**操作步骤**：
278	
279	1. 进入仓库根目录，执行：
280	
281	   ```bash
282	   git log --oneline -20
283	   ```
284	
285	2. 把输出按主题分组。分组线索：提交信息开头的方括号标签（`[Hybrid Engine]`、`[AutoEP]`、`[AffineIR]`、`[VocabTP]`）和前缀（`ZeRO-1/2:`、`ZeRO-3:`、`ci:`）。
286	3. 打开 [README.md:L27-L67](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L27-L67) 的 Latest News（含 More news），为每个分组找一条时间上最近的新闻佐证。
287	4. 用 `git log --oneline -20 -- deepspeed/runtime/zero/` 这样的路径过滤命令，分别统计各主题目录的提交热度。
288	5. 写成 1 页笔记，每个方向包含：方向名、证据提交（哈希 + 一句话）、README 佐证新闻（日期 + 标题）、一句话判断它解决的是显存墙 / 通信墙 / 吞吐中的哪一个。
289	
290	**参考范例**（以下为撰写本讲时对 HEAD `dc046b15d` 的真实观察，可作为你的笔记样例）：
291	
292	- **ZeRO 卸载与显存优化**：`dc046b15d`「ZeRO-1/2: preserve gradients across request boundaries until step」、`c6291b7e1`「ZeRO-3: copy offloaded master weights back to the device through pinned buffer」——佐证新闻：SuperOffload 获 ASPLOS 2026 提名（2026/03）、ZenFlow（2025/08）。主攻**显存墙**。

296	**需要观察的现象**：git log 的主题分布与 README 新闻的优先级高度吻合——新闻是「宣言」，提交是「行动」；两者不一致的地方（例如某特性上了新闻但近期无提交）通常意味着该方向已进入稳定维护期。

298	**预期结果**：一份含 3 个方向、每个方向有提交证据 + 新闻佐证 + 一句话定位的 1 页笔记。完成后建议存档在 `DeepSpeed-tutorial/` 之外的自有笔记目录里，学习单元 5 和单元 6 时回头验证你的判断。
299	
300	## 6. 本讲小结
301	
302	- DeepSpeed 是面向超大模型训练与推理的**底层优化库**，三大痛点是**显存墙、通信墙、训练吞吐**；核心创新包括 ZeRO、ZeRO-Infinity、3D 并行、Ulysses 序列并行与 DeepSpeed-MoE（[README.md:L71-L73](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L71-L73)）。
303	- README 的板块结构本身就是一张能力矩阵：News 看方向、Adoption 看生态（Transformers/Accelerate/Lightning 都在集成它）、CI 与 HW 表看硬件版图（NVIDIA/AMD/CPU/Gaudi/XPU/昇腾等）。

# DeepSpeed 项目全景：大模型训练为什么需要它

> 本讲是整本学习手册的第一讲。你不写一行 DeepSpeed 代码，只需要建立三样东西：对项目定位的认知、对文档地图的熟悉、对版本机制的把握。它们是后续所有源码阅读的坐标系。

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说清楚 DeepSpeed 解决的三大核心痛点：**显存墙**（模型放不进显存）、**通信墙**（多卡之间数据搬运太慢）、**训练吞吐**（整体训练太慢）。
2. 列举 DeepSpeed 的代表性系统创新：**ZeRO**、**ZeRO-Infinity / ZeRO-Offload**、**3D-Parallelism**、**Ulysses 序列并行**、**DeepSpeed-MoE** 等。
3. 知道仓库当前版本（0.19.9）、文档入口（deepspeed.ai 与 `docs/` 目录），以及它与 HuggingFace Transformers / Accelerate / Lightning 等框架的集成关系。
4. 学会用 `git log` 观察一个开源项目「最近在忙什么」，把 README 的新闻列表和实际代码提交互相印证。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲几乎不需要分布式训练背景，但以下概念会反复出现，先用大白话解释：

- **参数量 Ψ（psi）**：模型里所有可训练权重标量的总数。一个 7B 模型有约 70 亿个参数。显存讨论中常用 Ψ 代指「参数个数」。
- **数据并行（Data Parallelism, DP）**：每张卡都持有**完整的**模型副本，各自吃不同批次的数据，反向传播后同步梯度。最易用，但每张卡都重复存一份模型状态——这就是显存浪费的根源。
- **显存墙（memory wall）**：以混合精度 + Adam 优化器为例，除了参数本身，还要存梯度和优化器状态（Adam 的一阶/二阶动量、fp32 主权重）。粗略估算，训练状态约占

  \[ 2\Psi(\text{fp16 参数}) + 2\Psi(\text{fp16 梯度}) + 12\Psi(\text{fp32 优化器状态}) = 16\Psi \text{ 字节} \]

  一个 7B 模型仅模型状态就需要约 112 GB，而单卡显存通常只有 40~96 GB——模型还没跑起来就「撞墙」了。
- **通信墙（communication wall）**：多卡训练要在卡间搬运梯度/参数。当通信时间接近甚至超过计算时间，加卡不再提速。
- **ZeRO（Zero Redundancy Optimizer）**：DeepSpeed 的招牌技术。核心想法一句话：数据并行下每张卡都存了**完整副本**，这是冗余的；ZeRO 把优化器状态、梯度、参数逐级**切分**到各卡上，用时再临时聚合，从而用「通信换显存」。细节在单元 5 展开，本讲只需记住它是 DeepSpeed 的立身之本。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

本讲涉及的文件很少，都是「项目门面」级别的文件：

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `README.md` | 项目第一入口：新闻、定位、集成生态、硬件支持表、安装方式、论文列表 |
| `docs/_pages/training.md` | 官网「训练总览」页面的源文件，相当于官方版能力矩阵与特性清单 |
| `version.txt` | 单行文件，记录当前版本号（0.19.9），是发布线的源头 |
| `setup.py` | 安装脚本，从这里消费 `version.txt` |
| `deepspeed/__init__.py` | 主包入口，把版本号暴露为 `deepspeed.__version__` |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 README 的能力矩阵

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

读一个大型开源项目的第一步不是看代码，而是读它的 README，并从中提炼出一张「能力矩阵」：**它解决什么问题、靠什么技术解决、和谁协作、支持什么硬件**。

DeepSpeed 的 README 把这些信息分散在几个板块里：

| README 板块 | 回答的问题 |
| --- | --- |
| Latest News（L27 起） | 项目最近在往哪个方向演进 |
| Extreme Speed and Scale（L71 起） | 项目一句话定位与核心创新点 |
| DeepSpeed Adoption（L79 起） | 哪些著名大模型用它训出来、与哪些框架集成 |
| Build Pipeline Status（L110 起） | 在哪些硬件平台上跑 CI（即官方背书的平台） |
| Installation / HW support（L123 起） | 怎么装、支持哪些加速器 |
| Publications（L223 起） | 每项技术对应的论文 |

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

把 README 当地图来「测绘」的流程：

1. 先看定位句（Extreme Speed and Scale 段），抓住核心创新关键词。
2. 再看 Latest News，按时间倒序扫一遍，找出反复出现的主题（这些就是活跃战线）。
3. 然后看 Adoption 与集成表，确认生态位：它是「库」，被上层框架调用，而不是取代它们。
4. 最后看 Build Pipeline / HW support 表，确认硬件矩阵，这决定了后续读源码时会遇到的多后端抽象（单元 3 会讲）。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**① 一句话定位与五大创新点。** README 在标题段直接列出了 DeepSpeed 的系统创新清单：

> 这些创新包括 ZeRO、ZeRO-Infinity、3D-Parallelism、Ulysses Sequence Parallelism、DeepSpeed-MoE 等。

见 [README.md:L71-L73](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L71-L73)。这段话就是整本学习手册的「课程大纲」：单元 5 讲 ZeRO 系列，单元 6 讲 3D 并行 / Ulysses / MoE。README 还点出 DeepSpeed 训练过 MT-530B、BLOOM 等当时的最大模型，见 [README.md:L84-L95](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L84-L95)。

**② Latest News：项目的活跃战线。** 新闻列表从 2026/05 一直排到 2025/06，见 [README.md:L27-L51](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L27-L51)。几个值得记住的条目：

- Muon 优化器支持与 ZeRO-3 的 SDMA 卸载（2026/05，L29-L31）；
- SuperOffload 获 ASPLOS 2026 最佳论文提名（2026/03，L35）；
- Core API 更新：PyTorch 风格 backward 与低精度主权重（2025/12，L37）；
- ZenFlow 无停顿卸载引擎（2025/08，L47）。

折叠区「More news」里还有三条：DeepCompile（编译优化）、AutoTP（自动张量并行）、Ulysses-Offload（长上下文），见 [README.md:L55-L67](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L55-L67)。这些名字后续单元都会对应到具体源码目录（如 `deepspeed/compile/`、`deepspeed/module_inject/auto_tp.py`、`deepspeed/runtime/zenflow/`）。

**③ 集成生态：DeepSpeed 是「被集成」的库。** README 用一张表列出与主流框架的集成文档，见 [README.md:L97-L106](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L97-L106)：

- HuggingFace **Transformers**（L101）——最常见用法：`TrainingArguments` 里打开 `deepspeed` 即可；
- HuggingFace **Accelerate**（L102）；
- PyTorch **Lightning**、**MosaicML**、**Determined**、**MMEngine**（L103-L106）。

这说明 DeepSpeed 的生态位是**底层训练加速库**：用户通常不直接面对它，而是通过这些上层框架间接使用。但要看懂它为什么快、为什么省显存，必须回到源码——这正是本手册的目的。

**④ 硬件能力矩阵。** CI 表见 [README.md:L110-L121](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L110-L121)：NVIDIA、AMD、CPU、Intel Gaudi（hpu）、Intel XPU、华为昇腾 NPU 都有独立 CI。社区贡献的硬件表见 [README.md:L141-L151](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L141-L151)，列出各加速器的短名（`npu`、`hpu`、`cpu`、`xpu`、`sdaa`、`klxpu`）。这张表解释了为什么源码里会有一整套「加速器抽象层」（`deepspeed/accelerator/`，单元 3 精读）：一套代码要同时跑在这么多硬件上。

**⑤ 论文索引。** [README.md:L223-L262](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L223-L262) 的 Publications 列表是按技术查论文的入口：ZeRO 原论文（L224）、ZeRO-Infinity（L229）、DeepSpeed-MoE（L233）、ZeRO++（L245）、ZenFlow（L260）、SuperOffload（L262）等。读源码卡住时，回这里找对应论文往往能豁然开朗。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：亲手从 README 提炼出一张属于自己的能力矩阵表。

**操作步骤**：

1. 打开仓库根目录的 `README.md`（本讲用 HEAD `dc046b15d` 的版本）。
2. 用编辑器搜索以下小标题并记下其起始行号：`Latest News`、`Extreme Speed`、`DeepSpeed Adoption`、`Build Pipeline Status`、`Installation`、`Contributed HW support`、`Publications`。
3. 为每个板块用一句话总结它回答的问题，填进 4.1.1 的表格里替换掉我们的答案。
4. 统计 Latest News 中 2025-2026 年条目里出现次数最多的技术关键词（提示：offload/ZenFlow/SuperOffload 相关条目出现了 4 次以上）。

**需要观察的现象**：你会发现 README 的新闻列表不是随机罗列——offload（卸载）方向（ZeRO-Offload → ZeRO-Infinity → ZenFlow → SuperOffload）和并行方向（3D → AutoTP → AutoEP）各自成线，每条线都能在 Publications 里找到对应论文、在源码目录里找到对应模块。

**预期结果**：得到一张 7 行左右的能力矩阵表，并且能回答「DeepSpeed 最近一年最重要的三个新方向是什么」。如果答案里包含「卸载引擎（ZenFlow/SuperOffload）」「自动并行注入（AutoTP/AutoEP）」「编译优化（DeepCompile）」之一，说明读对了。

答案：ZeRO、ZeRO-Infinity、3D-Parallelism、Ulysses 序列并行、DeepSpeed-MoE（见 [README.md:L73](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L73)）。对应关系：ZeRO → 单元 5；3D 并行与 Ulysses → 单元 6；MoE → 单元 6；ZeRO-Infinity（NVMe 交换）→ 单元 5 第 7 讲。

### 4.2 训练文档结构

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`docs/` 目录是 DeepSpeed 官网（deepspeed.ai）的源文件，用 Jekyll 构建。其中 `docs/_pages/training.md` 是官网「Training Overview and Features」页面的源文件——可以把它理解为**官方版能力矩阵**：README 用一段话告诉你「有什么」，training.md 用整篇文档告诉你「每项特性具体是什么、怎么开」。

这个文件有个有趣的细节：它实际上包含**两个 Jekyll 页面**（两段 front matter），前半部分是 `/training/`（训练总览），后半部分是 `/features/`（特性详解）。读它时要意识到自己在「两页文档」之间穿越。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

training.md 的叙事结构本身就是一条问题-方案链，推荐按这个顺序读：

```
训练大模型难（Overview, L9-17）
  ├─ 要自己搭分布式/混合精度/梯度累积/检查点 → DeepSpeed API 轻量包装 PyTorch（L19-27）
  ├─ 太慢 → Speed：BERT-large 44 分钟、GPT-2 3.75x（L29-52）
  ├─ 显存不够 → Memory efficiency：ZeRO、ZeRO-Offload（L56-77）
  ├─ 规模上天 → Scalability：3D 并行、万亿参数（L79-96）
  ├─ 网络带宽差 → Communication efficiency：流水线并行降通信（L98-100）
  ├─ 数据太多 → Data efficiency：课程学习、token dropping（L102-103）
  ├─ 收敛太慢 → LAMB 等大 batch 优化器（L105-111）
  └─ 都想要但怕难用 → Good usability：几行代码接入（L114-115）
```

前半部分以「叙事」收尾于一张特性清单（L118-163）；后半部分（L165 起）逐项展开每个特性的细节与配置片段。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**① 问题描述：为什么需要 DeepSpeed。** 文档开篇直接点出双重痛点——既要搭好分布式/混合精度这些「样板代码」，又可能得不到理想的性能；大模型在纯数据并行下显存直接爆掉，而模型并行又难用：

见 [training.md:L9-L17](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L9-L17)。这句「a large model easily runs out of memory with pure data parallelism」就是第 2 节讲的显存墙的官方表述。

**② 产品哲学：轻量包装，不另起炉灶。** DeepSpeed API 被定位为「PyTorch 之上的轻量包装」——你仍用 PyTorch 的一切，DeepSpeed 接管分布式训练、混合精度、梯度累积、检查点这些样板技术，见 [training.md:L19-L27](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L19-L27)。这解释了为什么手册单元 2 讲 `initialize()` 时你会看到：模型、优化器、数据加载器都还是 PyTorch 对象，DeepSpeed 只是「包」了一层引擎。

**③ 显存效率：ZeRO 的官方定义。** 文档给出了 ZeRO 的一句话定义——与普通数据并行「复制」模型状态不同，ZeRO 把模型状态和梯度「切分」到各数据并行进程上，见 [training.md:L62-L69](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L62-L69)。同一节还给出量化对比：单卡 13B 参数 vs 传统 DDP 约 1.4B 就 OOM（L57-L60），ZeRO-2 最多省 8 倍内存（L66-L67）；ZeRO-Offload 进一步用「单张 V100 训 13B」打开局面，见 [training.md:L77](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L77)。

**④ 可扩展性与 3D 并行。** 「3D 并行」= 数据并行 + 张量并行 + 流水线并行三者组合，官方文档说明它支撑过万亿参数模型，见 [training.md:L79-L88](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L79-L88)。这三个维度分别对应单元 5（ZeRO 数据并行）、单元 6（张量/序列并行、流水线并行）。

**⑤ 核心 API 清单。** 文档后半部分总结了 DeepSpeed 的核心 API，只有寥寥几个方法：`initialize`、`backward`、`step`、`add_config_arguments`、`load_checkpoint` / `store_checkpoint`，见 [training.md:L305-L314](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L305-L314)。这是单元 2 的预习提纲：整个训练引擎对用户暴露的入口就这么几个。

**⑥ 特性深读区（后半页）。** 从 [training.md:L233-L259](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L233-L259) 开始逐项解释 ZeRO 的子优化（优化器状态与梯度切分、激活切分、恒定缓冲区优化 CBO、连续内存优化 CMO）——这四个名词在单元 5 读 `stage_1_and_2.py` / `stage3.py` 时会一一对应到具体代码。ZeRO-Offload 的展开说明见 [training.md:L279-L283](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L279-L283)。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：training.md 中 ZeRO 的官方一句话定义是什么？它和数据并行的本质区别在哪里？

答案：ZeRO 与「在数据并行进程间复制内存状态」的基本数据并行不同，它把模型状态（model states）和梯度**切分（partition）**到各进程以节省内存（见 [training.md:L62-L65](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L62-L65)）。本质区别：复制 vs 切分——切分换来的是显存节省，付出的是用时需临时通信聚合。

**练习 2**：文档说 DeepSpeed 的核心 API「只有一把手能数得过来的几个方法」，请列举它们。

答案：`initialize`（初始化）、`backward` 和 `step`（训练）、`add_config_arguments`（参数解析）、`load_checkpoint` 和 `store_checkpoint`（检查点），见 [training.md:L305-L310](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L305-L310)。

**练习 3**：「3D 并行」中的三个维度是什么？ZeRO 在其中扮演哪个维度？

答案：数据并行、张量/模型并行、流水线并行（见 [training.md:L80-L82](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/docs/_pages/training.md#L80-L82)）。ZeRO 强化的是数据并行这一维（内存高效的数据并行），且可与另外两类并行组合。

### 4.3 版本与发布线

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

「这个仓库现在是哪个版本？」看似简单，但在 DeepSpeed 里版本信息有一条清晰的**传递链**：

```
version.txt（唯一事实来源，当前 0.19.9）
   ├─→ setup.py 打包时读取 → PyPI 发布的包版本
   └─→ (构建期写入) deepspeed/git_version_info.py
          └─→ deepspeed/__init__.py 导出 __version__ / __git_hash__ / __git_branch__
```

理解这条链的意义在于：**用户看到的 `deepspeed.__version__` 与仓库里的 `version.txt` 是同源的**；而且 DeepSpeed 还把 git 提交哈希打进包里，运行时日志会打印 version + git-hash + git-branch，这对你排查「线上到底跑的是哪份代码」极其有用（阅读源码时也能用它确认代码与讲义引用的 HEAD 一致）。

另一个要点是**发布节奏**：DeepSpeed 是「rolling master」模式——master 分支持续合入，定期打 tag 发 PyPI。所以 `git log` 里的最新提交就是最真实的项目动态，比新闻列表更细粒度。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

版本信息的生命周期：

1. 开发期：`version.txt` 由维护者更新，`0.19.9` 表示主版本 0、次版本 19、补丁版本 9。
2. 构建期：`setup.py` 读取 `version.txt`；如果设置了 `DS_BUILD_STRING` 环境变量则附加 `.devX` 后缀，否则把 git 哈希写入版本串，并生成 `deepspeed/git_version_info.py`。
3. 运行期：`import deepspeed` 时从 `git_version_info` 导入 version / git_hash / git_branch，暴露为 `deepspeed.__version__`、`deepspeed.__git_hash__`。
4. 日志期：每次 `initialize()` 都会打印 `DeepSpeed info: version=..., git-hash=..., git-branch=...`。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**① 唯一事实来源：version.txt。** 整个文件只有一行：

见 [version.txt:L1](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/version.txt#L1)——内容就是 `0.19.9`。这就是本手册撰写时仓库的版本号，也就是大纲中所说的 v0.19.9。

**② setup.py 消费版本号。** 安装脚本在打包时读取该文件：

见 [setup.py:L228-L229](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/setup.py#L228-L229)，注释明确写着「Parse the DeepSpeed version string from version.txt」。紧随其后（L231 起）的逻辑决定是否附加 `.dev` 后缀或 git 哈希。

**③ 包入口导出版本三元组与 git 信息。** `import deepspeed` 时：

见 [deepspeed/__init__.py:L70](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L70)，从 `git_version_info`（构建时生成）导入 version、git_hash、git_branch；随后在 [deepspeed/__init__.py:L75-L85](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L75-L85) 解析出主/次/补丁三元组并导出 `__version__`、`__git_hash__`、`__git_branch__`。同一个文件里，[deepspeed/__init__.py:L88](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L88) 附近的 `dist = None` 是个伏笔：分布式通信句柄被设计为延迟绑定（引擎初始化时才指向 `deepspeed.comm`），单元 3 会展开。

顺带一提，`deepspeed/__init__.py:498` 与 `721` 附近各有一行 `log_dist("DeepSpeed info: version={}, git-hash={}, git-branch={}"...)`——这就是运行时日志里版本行的出处。

#### 4.3.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：验证版本传递链的三环都指向同一个版本号。

**操作步骤**：

1. `cat version.txt` → 记下输出（预期 `0.19.9`）。
2. `grep -n "version.txt" setup.py` → 确认 setup.py 第 229 行在读取它。
3. 若本地已安装 deepspeed：`python -c "import deepspeed; print(deepspeed.__version__, deepspeed.__git_hash__)"` → 对比输出与第 1 步结果，并核对 `__git_hash__` 的前 9 位是否等于 `git rev-parse --short=9 HEAD`（本仓库 HEAD 为 `dc046b15d`）。
4. `pip index versions deepspeed 2>/dev/null || pip install deepspeed==` → 观察 PyPI 上可用的版本列表，看看 0.19.9 处在发布线的什么位置。

**需要观察的现象**：第 3 步中 `__version__` 与 `version.txt` 一致；若你是 `pip install deepspeed` 装的正式发行版，`__git_hash__` 是打包那次提交的哈希；若是源码 editable 安装（`pip install -e .`），哈希应与你本地 HEAD 一致。

**预期结果**：三个环节读出的版本号完全一致。第 3、4 步依赖本地 Python 环境，**待本地验证**。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：DeepSpeed 的版本号「唯一事实来源」是哪个文件？当前值是多少？

答案：仓库根目录的 `version.txt`，当前值为 `0.19.9`（见 [version.txt:L1](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/version.txt#L1)）。

**练习 2**：为什么 `deepspeed.__version__` 之外还要导出 `__git_hash__`？举一个实际用途。

答案：因为 PyPI 版本号更新有间隔，而 rolling master 每天都有合入，仅凭 `0.19.9` 无法区分「同一版本号下不同的代码状态」。`__git_hash__`（见 [deepspeed/__init__.py:L84](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/deepspeed/__init__.py#L84)）能精确定位到具体提交。实际用途：报 bug 时把 `initialize()` 日志里的 version/git-hash 行贴出来，维护者即可复现你的代码版本；本手册也用它保证所有永久链接指向同一提交。

**练习 3**：如果不小心删除了 `version.txt`，安装（`pip install -e .`）会在哪一步失败？

答案：在 `setup.py` 执行到 [setup.py:L229](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/setup.py#L229) 的 `open('version.txt', 'r')` 时直接抛 `FileNotFoundError`，打包元数据无法生成。这体现了该文件作为唯一事实来源的地位。

## 5. 综合实践

**任务：写一份 1 页的《DeepSpeed 活跃方向调研笔记》——用 git 历史与 README 新闻互相印证。**

一份开源项目的「自我介绍」（README News）和它的「实际行为」（git log）对照着读，是判断项目健康度和方向的最快方法。本实践把前面三个模块串起来。

**实践目标**：从真实提交记录中识别出 3 个正在积极演进的子系统，并与 README 的 Latest News 互相印证。

**操作步骤**：

1. 进入仓库根目录，执行：

   ```bash
   git log --oneline -20
   ```

2. 把输出按主题分组。分组线索：提交信息开头的方括号标签（`[Hybrid Engine]`、`[AutoEP]`、`[AffineIR]`、`[VocabTP]`）和前缀（`ZeRO-1/2:`、`ZeRO-3:`、`ci:`）。
3. 打开 [README.md:L27-L67](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L27-L67) 的 Latest News（含 More news），为每个分组找一条时间上最近的新闻佐证。
4. 用 `git log --oneline -20 -- deepspeed/runtime/zero/` 这样的路径过滤命令，分别统计各主题目录的提交热度。
5. 写成 1 页笔记，每个方向包含：方向名、证据提交（哈希 + 一句话）、README 佐证新闻（日期 + 标题）、一句话判断它解决的是显存墙 / 通信墙 / 吞吐中的哪一个。

**参考范例**（以下为撰写本讲时对 HEAD `dc046b15d` 的真实观察，可作为你的笔记样例）：

- **ZeRO 卸载与显存优化**：`dc046b15d`「ZeRO-1/2: preserve gradients across request boundaries until step」、`c6291b7e1`「ZeRO-3: copy offloaded master weights back to the device through pinned buffer」——佐证新闻：SuperOffload 获 ASPLOS 2026 提名（2026/03）、ZenFlow（2025/08）。主攻**显存墙**。
- **专家并行 AutoEP / AffineIR**：`66fef47b2`、`f81850499`、`12ffb9903`、`7501610ee` 四条 AutoEP/AffineIR 相关提交——佐证新闻：Ray x DeepSpeed Meetup 中提到的专家并行与 fused kernel 工作（2025/10）。主攻**吞吐与显存**。
- **混合引擎与张量并行**：`ab7fd98fa`「[Hybrid Engine] Enable graph capture ... on non-CUDA accelerators」、`1a956270f`「[VocabTP] vocab_parallel_ce support fused LM-head projection + loss」——佐证新闻：AutoTP（2025/03，More news）。主攻**推理/训练一体化与通信墙**。

**需要观察的现象**：git log 的主题分布与 README 新闻的优先级高度吻合——新闻是「宣言」，提交是「行动」；两者不一致的地方（例如某特性上了新闻但近期无提交）通常意味着该方向已进入稳定维护期。

**预期结果**：一份含 3 个方向、每个方向有提交证据 + 新闻佐证 + 一句话定位的 1 页笔记。完成后建议存档在 `DeepSpeed-tutorial/` 之外的自有笔记目录里，学习单元 5 和单元 6 时回头验证你的判断。

## 6. 本讲小结

- DeepSpeed 是面向超大模型训练与推理的**底层优化库**，三大痛点是**显存墙、通信墙、训练吞吐**；核心创新包括 ZeRO、ZeRO-Infinity、3D 并行、Ulysses 序列并行与 DeepSpeed-MoE（[README.md:L71-L73](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L71-L73)）。
- README 的板块结构本身就是一张能力矩阵：News 看方向、Adoption 看生态（Transformers/Accelerate/Lightning 都在集成它）、CI 与 HW 表看硬件版图（NVIDIA/AMD/CPU/Gaudi/XPU/昇腾等）。
- `docs/_pages/training.md` 是官方能力矩阵的展开版：按「难 → 快 → 省 → 大 → 通 → 效 → 易」的问题链组织；其中 ZeRO 的定义（切分而非复制）与核心 API 清单（`initialize`/`backward`/`step`/checkpoint）是单元 2 的直接预习材料。
- 版本传递链：`version.txt`（0.19.9）→ `setup.py` 打包 → `deepspeed.__version__` / `__git_hash__`；运行时日志会打印 version + git-hash + git-branch，用于精确定位代码版本。
- 阅读 »README News + git log« 双轨对照是判断开源项目活跃方向的标准手法；当前最活跃的三条线是 ZeRO 卸载（ZenFlow/SuperOffload 系）、专家并行（AutoEP/AffineIR）、混合引擎/张量并行。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

下一讲（u1-l2「代码地图：仓库目录结构与模块导览」）将钻进 `deepspeed/` 主包，逐一认识 runtime、ops、module_inject、csrc 等目录的职责分工，并精读 `deepspeed/__init__.py` 的导出列表。在进入下一讲之前，建议你：

1. 把本讲的「文档小节 ↔ 源码目录」对照表再过一遍，下一讲会把每个目录展开讲。
2. 通读一遍 [README.md:L123-L169](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/dc046b15d7a58f6c8dacba435508b52b1ebc620c/README.md#L123-L169) 的安装章节，留意「JIT 编译」与「预编译」两种算子构建方式的区别——这是 u1-l3 的主题。

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind.
